scene.label: Act 3, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Another part of the island.

content.text: Enter Caliban with a bottle, Stephano and Trinculo.

lines.text: Tell not me:—when the butt is out we will drink water; not a drop before: therefore bear up, and board 'em. Servant-monster, drink to me.
lines.plainText: Tell not mewhen the butt is out we will drink water not a drop before therefore bear up and board 'em Servantmonster drink to me

lines.text: Servant-monster! The folly of this island! They say there's but five upon this isle; we are three of them; if th' other two be brained like us, the state totters.
lines.plainText: Servantmonster The folly of this island They say there's but five upon this isle we are three of them if th' other two be brained like us the state totters

lines.text: Drink, servant-monster, when I bid thee: thy eyes are almost set in thy head.
lines.plainText: Drink servantmonster when I bid thee thy eyes are almost set in thy head

lines.text: Where should they be set else? He were a brave monster indeed, if they were set in his tail.
lines.plainText: Where should they be set else He were a brave monster indeed if they were set in his tail

lines.text: My man-monster hath drown'd his tongue in sack: for my part, the sea cannot drown me; I swam, ere I could recover the shore, five-and-thirty leagues, off and on, by this light. Thou shalt be my lieutenant, monster, or my standard.
lines.plainText: My manmonster hath drown'd his tongue in sack for my part the sea cannot drown me I swam ere I could recover the shore fiveandthirty leagues off and on by this light Thou shalt be my lieutenant monster or my standard

lines.text: Your lieutenant, if you list; he's no standard.
lines.plainText: Your lieutenant if you list he's no standard

lines.text: We'll not run, Monsieur monster.
lines.plainText: We'll not run Monsieur monster

lines.text: Nor go neither. But you'll lie like dogs, and yet say nothing neither.
lines.plainText: Nor go neither But you'll lie like dogs and yet say nothing neither

lines.text: Moon-calf, speak once in thy life, if thou beest a good moon-calf.
lines.plainText: Mooncalf speak once in thy life if thou beest a good mooncalf

lines.text: How does thy honour? Let me lick thy shoe. I'll not serve him, he is not valiant.
lines.plainText: How does thy honour Let me lick thy shoe I'll not serve him he is not valiant

lines.text: Thou liest, most ignorant monster: I am in case to justle a constable. Why, thou deboshed fish thou, was there ever man a coward that hath drunk so much sack as I today? Wilt thou tell a monstrous lie, being but half a fish and half a monster?
lines.plainText: Thou liest most ignorant monster I am in case to justle a constable Why thou deboshed fish thou was there ever man a coward that hath drunk so much sack as I today Wilt thou tell a monstrous lie being but half a fish and half a monster

lines.text: Lo, how he mocks me! wilt thou let him, my lord?
lines.plainText: Lo how he mocks me wilt thou let him my lord

lines.text: "Lord" quoth he! That a monster should be such a natural!
lines.plainText: Lord quoth he That a monster should be such a natural

lines.text: Lo, lo again! bite him to death, I prithee.
lines.plainText: Lo lo again bite him to death I prithee

lines.text: Trinculo, keep a good tongue in your head: if you prove a mutineer, the next tree! The poor monster's my subject, and he shall not suffer indignity.
lines.plainText: Trinculo keep a good tongue in your head if you prove a mutineer the next tree The poor monster's my subject and he shall not suffer indignity

lines.text: I thank my noble lord. Wilt thou be pleas'd to hearken once again to the suit I made to thee?
lines.plainText: I thank my noble lord Wilt thou be pleas'd to hearken once again to the suit I made to thee

lines.text: Marry. will I. Kneel and repeat it. I will stand, and so shall Trinculo.
lines.plainText: Marry will I Kneel and repeat it I will stand and so shall Trinculo

lines.text: As I told thee before, I am subject to a tyrant, a sorcerer, that by his cunning hath cheated me of the island.
lines.plainText: As I told thee before I am subject to a tyrant a sorcerer that by his cunning hath cheated me of the island

lines.text: Thou liest.
lines.plainText: Thou liest

lines.text: Thou liest, thou jesting monkey, thou;
lines.plainText: Thou liest thou jesting monkey thou

lines.text: I would my valiant master would destroy thee;
lines.plainText: I would my valiant master would destroy thee

lines.text: I do not lie.
lines.plainText: I do not lie

lines.text: Trinculo, if you trouble him any more in his tale, by this hand, I will supplant some of your teeth.
lines.plainText: Trinculo if you trouble him any more in his tale by this hand I will supplant some of your teeth

lines.text: Why, I said nothing.
lines.plainText: Why I said nothing

lines.text: Mum, then, and no more. Proceed.
lines.plainText: Mum then and no more Proceed

lines.text: I say, by sorcery he got this isle;
lines.plainText: I say by sorcery he got this isle

lines.text: From me he got it. If thy greatness will,
lines.plainText: From me he got it If thy greatness will

lines.text: Revenge it on him,—for I know thou dar'st;
lines.plainText: Revenge it on himfor I know thou dar'st

lines.text: But this thing dare not,—
lines.plainText: But this thing dare not

lines.text: That's most certain.
lines.plainText: That's most certain

lines.text: Thou shalt be lord of it and I'll serve thee.
lines.plainText: Thou shalt be lord of it and I'll serve thee

lines.text: How now shall this be compassed? Canst thou bring me to the party?
lines.plainText: How now shall this be compassed Canst thou bring me to the party

lines.text: Yea, yea, my lord: I'll yield him thee asleep,
lines.plainText: Yea yea my lord I'll yield him thee asleep

lines.text: Where thou mayst knock a nail into his head.
lines.plainText: Where thou mayst knock a nail into his head

lines.text: Thou liest. Thou canst not.
lines.plainText: Thou liest Thou canst not

lines.text: What a pied ninny's this! Thou scurvy patch!
lines.plainText: What a pied ninny's this Thou scurvy patch

lines.text: I do beseech thy greatness, give him blows,
lines.plainText: I do beseech thy greatness give him blows

lines.text: And take his bottle from him: when that's gone
lines.plainText: And take his bottle from him when that's gone

lines.text: He shall drink nought but brine; for I'll not show him
lines.plainText: He shall drink nought but brine for I'll not show him

lines.text: Where the quick freshes are.
lines.plainText: Where the quick freshes are

lines.text: Trinculo, run into no further danger: interrupt the monster one word further, and by this hand, I'll turn my mercy out o' doors, and make a stock-fish of thee.
lines.plainText: Trinculo run into no further danger interrupt the monster one word further and by this hand I'll turn my mercy out o' doors and make a stockfish of thee

lines.text: Why, what did I? I did nothing. I'll go farther off.
lines.plainText: Why what did I I did nothing I'll go farther off

lines.text: Didst thou not say he lied?
lines.plainText: Didst thou not say he lied

lines.text: Thou liest.
lines.plainText: Thou liest

lines.text: Do I so? Take thou that.
lines.plainText: Do I so Take thou that

lines.text: I did not give the lie. Out o' your wits and hearing too? A pox o' your bottle! this can sack and drinking do. A murrain on your monster, and the devil take your fingers!
lines.plainText: I did not give the lie Out o' your wits and hearing too A pox o' your bottle this can sack and drinking do A murrain on your monster and the devil take your fingers

lines.text: Ha, ha, ha!
lines.plainText: Ha ha ha

lines.text: Now, forward with your tale.—Prithee stand further off.
lines.plainText: Now forward with your talePrithee stand further off

lines.text: Beat him enough: after a little time,
lines.plainText: Beat him enough after a little time

lines.text: I'll beat him too.
lines.plainText: I'll beat him too

lines.text: Stand farther.—Come, proceed.
lines.plainText: Stand fartherCome proceed

lines.text: Why, as I told thee, 'tis a custom with him
lines.plainText: Why as I told thee 'tis a custom with him

lines.text: I' th' afternoon to sleep: there thou mayst brain him,
lines.plainText: I' th' afternoon to sleep there thou mayst brain him

lines.text: Having first seiz'd his books; or with a log
lines.plainText: Having first seiz'd his books or with a log

lines.text: Batter his skull, or paunch him with a stake,
lines.plainText: Batter his skull or paunch him with a stake

lines.text: Or cut his wezand with thy knife. Remember
lines.plainText: Or cut his wezand with thy knife Remember

lines.text: First to possess his books; for without them
lines.plainText: First to possess his books for without them

lines.text: He's but a sot, as I am, nor hath not
lines.plainText: He's but a sot as I am nor hath not

lines.text: One spirit to command: they all do hate him
lines.plainText: One spirit to command they all do hate him

lines.text: As rootedly as I. Burn but his books.
lines.plainText: As rootedly as I Burn but his books

lines.text: He has brave utensils,—for so he calls them,—
lines.plainText: He has brave utensilsfor so he calls them

lines.text: Which, when he has a house, he'll deck withal.
lines.plainText: Which when he has a house he'll deck withal

lines.text: And that most deeply to consider is
lines.plainText: And that most deeply to consider is

lines.text: The beauty of his daughter; he himself
lines.plainText: The beauty of his daughter he himself

lines.text: Calls her a nonpareil: I never saw a woman
lines.plainText: Calls her a nonpareil I never saw a woman

lines.text: But only Sycorax my dam and she;
lines.plainText: But only Sycorax my dam and she

lines.text: But she as far surpasseth Sycorax
lines.plainText: But she as far surpasseth Sycorax

lines.text: As great'st does least.
lines.plainText: As great'st does least

lines.text: Is it so brave a lass?
lines.plainText: Is it so brave a lass

lines.text: Ay, lord, she will become thy bed, I warrant,
lines.plainText: Ay lord she will become thy bed I warrant

lines.text: And bring thee forth brave brood.
lines.plainText: And bring thee forth brave brood

lines.text: Monster, I will kill this man. His daughter and I will be king and queen,—save our graces!—and Trinculo and thyself shall be viceroys. Dost thou like the plot, Trinculo?
lines.plainText: Monster I will kill this man His daughter and I will be king and queensave our gracesand Trinculo and thyself shall be viceroys Dost thou like the plot Trinculo

lines.text: Excellent.
lines.plainText: Excellent

lines.text: Give me thy hand: I am sorry I beat thee; but while thou liv'st, keep a good tongue in thy head.
lines.plainText: Give me thy hand I am sorry I beat thee but while thou liv'st keep a good tongue in thy head

lines.text: Within this half hour will he be asleep.
lines.plainText: Within this half hour will he be asleep

lines.text: Wilt thou destroy him then?
lines.plainText: Wilt thou destroy him then

lines.text: Ay, on mine honour.
lines.plainText: Ay on mine honour

lines.text: This will I tell my master.
lines.plainText: This will I tell my master

lines.text: Thou mak'st me merry. I am full of pleasure.
lines.plainText: Thou mak'st me merry I am full of pleasure

lines.text: Let us be jocund: will you troll the catch
lines.plainText: Let us be jocund will you troll the catch

lines.text: You taught me but while-ere?
lines.plainText: You taught me but whileere

lines.text: At thy request, monster, I will do reason, any reason. Come on, Trinculo, let us sing.
lines.plainText: At thy request monster I will do reason any reason Come on Trinculo let us sing

lines.text: That's not the tune.
lines.plainText: That's not the tune

content.text: [Ariel plays the tune on a tabor and pipe.]

lines.text: What is this same?
lines.plainText: What is this same

lines.text: This is the tune of our catch, played by the picture of Nobody.
lines.plainText: This is the tune of our catch played by the picture of Nobody

lines.text: If thou beest a man, show thyself in thy likeness: if thou beest a devil, take 't as thou list.
lines.plainText: If thou beest a man show thyself in thy likeness if thou beest a devil take 't as thou list

lines.text: O, forgive me my sins!
lines.plainText: O forgive me my sins

lines.text: He that dies pays all debts: I defy thee. Mercy upon us!
lines.plainText: He that dies pays all debts I defy thee Mercy upon us

lines.text: Art thou afeard?
lines.plainText: Art thou afeard

lines.text: No, monster, not I.
lines.plainText: No monster not I

lines.text: Be not afeard. The isle is full of noises,
lines.plainText: Be not afeard The isle is full of noises

lines.text: Sounds, and sweet airs, that give delight, and hurt not.
lines.plainText: Sounds and sweet airs that give delight and hurt not

lines.text: Sometimes a thousand twangling instruments
lines.plainText: Sometimes a thousand twangling instruments

lines.text: Will hum about mine ears; and sometimes voices,
lines.plainText: Will hum about mine ears and sometimes voices

lines.text: That, if I then had wak'd after long sleep,
lines.plainText: That if I then had wak'd after long sleep

lines.text: Will make me sleep again: and then, in dreaming,
lines.plainText: Will make me sleep again and then in dreaming

lines.text: The clouds methought would open and show riches
lines.plainText: The clouds methought would open and show riches

lines.text: Ready to drop upon me; that, when I wak'd,
lines.plainText: Ready to drop upon me that when I wak'd

lines.text: I cried to dream again.
lines.plainText: I cried to dream again

lines.text: This will prove a brave kingdom to me, where I shall have my music for nothing.
lines.plainText: This will prove a brave kingdom to me where I shall have my music for nothing

lines.text: When Prospero is destroyed.
lines.plainText: When Prospero is destroyed

lines.text: That shall be by and by: I remember the story.
lines.plainText: That shall be by and by I remember the story

lines.text: The sound is going away. Let's follow it, and after do our work.
lines.plainText: The sound is going away Let's follow it and after do our work

lines.text: Lead, monster: we'll follow. I would I could see this taborer! he lays it on. Wilt come?
lines.plainText: Lead monster we'll follow I would I could see this taborer he lays it on Wilt come

lines.text: I'll follow, Stephano.
lines.plainText: I'll follow Stephano
